docs.title: Home
docs.text:
PyFlange computes the bolt axial force and bolt bending moment of a flange segment as a function of the tower shell force, including the effect of flange gaps (flatness imperfections) and flange inclination. On top of this model it provides the bolt fatigue assessment of IEC 61400-6 and the tools for probabilistic (Monte Carlo) analyses.

It is meant for engineers who design or check the L-flanges and T-flanges of wind turbine towers, monopiles and transition pieces, and who need a fast, transparent and verifiable implementation of the standard.

from pyflange.flangesegments import PolynomialLFlangeSegment

fseg = PolynomialLFlangeSegment(a=0.150, b=0.122, s=0.054, t=0.172, R=4.0, ...)
Fs = fseg.bolt_axial_force(500e3)       # bolt force for a 500 kN shell force

docs.title: PyFlange
docs.text: Open-source Python library for the fatigue analysis of large bolted ring-flange connections, implementing the polynomial flange segment model of IEC 61400-6 AMD1.

docs.title: The Bolt & Beautiful project
docs.text:
PyFlange has been developed within Bolt & Beautiful, a GROW research project on the bolted connections of offshore wind turbine support structures, by KCI, Siemens Gamesa, JBO and TNO. The project is funded with subsidy from the Top Sector Energy of the Dutch Ministry of Economic Affairs.

Within the project, extensive finite element studies were carried out. They supported the calibration of the safety factors and small improvements of the analytical flange model, which are proposed for the next edition of IEC 61400-6 (ref. [5], section 1.1).

docs.title: The link with IEC 61400-6
docs.text:
IEC 61400-6 is the international standard for the design of wind turbine towers and foundations. Its amendment 1 (AMD1, published in June 2025) replaced the former Schmidt/Neuper approach for the fatigue design of flange bolts with a new analytical model, developed by Marc Seidel (Siemens Gamesa), which covers the effect of flange gaps of the size allowed by the manufacturing tolerances (ref. [1]). The model is given in Annex G.2 of the standard (ref. [2]), and the use of AMD1 becomes mandatory for IEC certification from December 2026 (ref. [5], section 9.2).

The model is considerably more complex than the previous one. To help the industry implement it, PyFlange was developed as an open-source reference implementation, and it is referred to in the background document of the standard (ref. [5], section 9.2). The results of PyFlange are verified against the reference spreadsheets of Siemens Gamesa (see Validation).

The revision of the standard towards Edition 2 (ED2) introduces some small changes to the model and new design gap heights (ref. [5], section 9.7). PyFlange implements them in separate classes (PolynomialLFlangeSegmentED2, PolynomialTFlangeSegmentED2, gap_height_distribution_ED2), so that both versions can be compared.

ED2 is a draft

The ED2 implementation follows the draft background document of 2026-08-04 (ref. [5]). It may change before ED2 is published. Use the AMD1 classes for certified designs.

The documents cited as ref. [n] throughout this documentation are listed on the References page.

docs.text: The notable changes of each PyFlange version. The complete history is available in the GitHub repository.

docs.title: 0.13.0 (unreleased)
docs.text:
• Model aligned with the published IEC 61400-6:2020+AMD1:2025: docstrings cite the published equation numbers; T-flange ULS failure modes D and E, initial slope bound and b'E corrected; exact cubic bolt moment for T-flanges (eq. G.61); Tobinaga & Ishihara correction applied only within its validity range.
  • T-flanges: preload losses (PPL, DFT, settlement_factor), callable k_shell, and tilt_angle is now a required argument.
  • New PolynomialTFlangeSegmentED2.
  • New JSON case format (version 0.2.0) and pyflange.io module.
  • New command-line interface: pyflange determ, sample, inspect, stats.
  • ED2 gap statistics: gap_height_distribution_ED2, gap_angle_distribution_ED2, standard_gap_sampler_ED2.
  • New samplers: product_sampler, clayton_copula_sampler, clayton_gap_sampler.
  • standard_hole_diameter; StandardMetricBolt accepts shank_diameter_ratio="pitch".
  • Automated validation against the SGRE reference workbooks.
  • New documentation website.
  • Removed utils.log_data and utils.read_data_log: the intermediate quantities of the flange segment models (kfac, ftot, Acf, Icf, u, kseg, Itg, FV,c, ...) are now private cached properties, computed on demand. The verbose JSON output no longer contains the gap_k_mean and gap_COV keys, which were always null.
• Documentation of README.md, bolts and fatigue improved.
• standard_gap_sampler: gap angles larger than 180° are discarded and drawn again.
• standard_gap_sampler: realizations with a gap height above the cap are discarded and drawn again, instead of being set to the 95% quantile.

• First draft of the ED2 L-flange model (PolynomialLFlangeSegmentED2).
  • New weibull_sampler and beta_sampler.

• Gap height cap of standard_gap_sampler as a parameter.
  • Stress multiplication factor in fatigue_case_sampler, constant or random.
  • Fixed reduce_to_pi.

• Stress multiplication factor (SMF) for the bolt stress ranges.
  • standard_bolt_fatigue_curve_sampler: mean reference stress range as a parameter.
  • Fixed the averaging of the bolt preloads in the flange segment sampler.
  • Removed markov_matrix_from_SGRE_format.
• Bolt preload losses due to settlement and plastic strain (PPL, DFT, settlement_factor) in PolynomialLFlangeSegment and in the flange segment sampler.
• Minor fixes and API documentation updates.
• New Gap class: the flange segment parameters gap_height, gap_angle and gap_shape_factor are replaced by a single gap parameter.

• New stats module, with probability distributions and random samplers for Monte Carlo simulations; gap module deprecated.
  • New BoltFatigueAnalysis class.
  • k_shell can be a function of the flange segment.

• New MarkovMatrix class, with an explicit load duration.
  • Failure mode D uses c' instead of c.

• Fixed the iterative calculation of failure modes D and E.
  • Fixed the initial slope of the L-flange bolt force curve.
• PolynomialTFlangeSegment.validate requires failure mode A instead of B.

• Documentation prepared for the public release.
  • Bolt, nut and washer databases moved to CSV files.

• Gap stiffness factor as a function of the gap angle.
  • Shell stiffness interpolated from FEA results (shell_stiffness).
  • bolt_markov_matrix function; BoltCrossSection class.

• New fatigue module with BoltFatigueCurve.
  • Washers and nuts in the flange segment models.
• PolynomialTFlangeSegment: gap shapes other than sinusoidal.
• PolynomialLFlangeSegment: flange tilt, validated against the SGRE reference implementation.
• First versions: polynomial L-flange segment model and bolts.

docs.title: Command-line interface
docs.text:
PyFlange includes a command-line tool that performs deterministic and Monte Carlo bolt fatigue analyses of flange cases described in the PyFlange JSON format, without writing any code. After installing PyFlange, it can be invoked either as pyflange or as py -m pyflange (python -m pyflange on Linux and macOS):

py -m pyflange --help
py -m pyflange COMMAND --help
py -m pyflange --version

Tip

py -m pyflange always works. The shorter pyflange works only if the folder of the Python scripts is in your PATH. The examples below use the short form.

A complete example case file is available here: fatigue-case.json. For a guided introduction, see First analysis without code and Monte Carlo from the command line.

Command Purpose determ Deterministic fatigue analysis of a case. sample Monte Carlo simulation of a case. inspect Detailed report of one realization of a Monte Carlo sample. stats Summary statistics of a Monte Carlo sample.

docs.title: determ
docs.text:
Performs a deterministic fatigue analysis and writes a detailed report of the case and its results to a JSON file (see Result files).

pyflange determ case.json                    # writes case-res.json
pyflange determ case.json --xlsx             # also writes case-res.xlsx
pyflange determ case.json --gap-angle 45 --gap-height 1.5 --tilt-angle 0.2 --smf 1.1
Option Description --gap-angle Override of the gap angle, in degrees. The shell stiffness is re-interpolated for the new angle. --gap-height Override of the gap height, in mm. --tilt-angle Override of the tilt angle, in degrees. --smf Stress multiplication factor. Defaults to the case SMF, or 1.0. --odir Output folder. Defaults to the current folder. --oname Output file name. Defaults to <case>-res[<overrides>].json. --xlsx Also write the report to an Excel file, as a key/value table with a named cell per value.

The main results in the report are damage, FatigueLife and, in the FlangeSegment section, BoltPreload, the polynomial points Point1 to Point4 and the curves TransferFunctions.

docs.title: sample
docs.text:
Runs a Monte Carlo simulation, based on the Stats section of the case, and writes one row per realization to a CSV file.

pyflange sample case.json                     # 100000 realizations, case-sample.csv
pyflange sample case.json --size 5000 --seed 1 --xlsx
Option Description --size Number of realizations. Defaults to 100000. --seed Seed of the random number generator. With the same seed and case, the same sample is generated. If omitted, every run is different. --odir Output folder. Defaults to the current folder. --oname Output file name. Defaults to <case>-sample.csv. --xlsx Also write the sample to an Excel file.

The CSV columns are:

Column Unit Description BoltPreload N Bolt preload after losses. GapShapeFactor - Gap shape factor. TiltAngle rad Flange tilt angle. GapAngle rad Gap angle. GapHeight m Gap height. FatigueClass Pa Knee-point stress range of the random bolt S-N curve (size effect included). MomentRangeCoefficient - Factor applied to the Markov matrix ranges. Damage - Fatigue damage. AllowableDamage - Allowable damage. FatigueLife as Markov matrix duration Fatigue life. SMF - Stress multiplication factor. Utilization - Damage / AllowableDamage.

The first column (without header) is the number of the realization, starting from 0, to be used with inspect.

docs.title: inspect
docs.text:
Rebuilds a single realization of a sample and writes its detailed report, like determ does for the deterministic case. This is useful to investigate outliers.

pyflange inspect case.json 1234               # reads case-sample.csv, writes case-realization-1234.json
pyflange inspect case.json 1234 --spath other-sample.csv --xlsx
Option Description --spath Path of the sample CSV file. Defaults to <case>-sample.csv, in the folder of the case. --odir, --oname, --xlsx As for determ.

docs.title: stats
docs.text:
Prints minimum, 5% quantile, average, 95% quantile, maximum, standard deviation and coefficient of variation of each column of a sample.

pyflange stats case-sample.csv

docs.title: Running batches
docs.text:
To analyze all the case files of a folder, use a loop of the Windows command prompt:

for %f in (*.json) do pyflange determ "%f" --odir results

(In a .bat file, write %%f instead of %f.) The results folder must exist; create it with mkdir results. Note that the loop also picks up the result files if they are written in the same folder as the cases.

In PowerShell:

Get-ChildItem *.json | ForEach-Object { pyflange determ $_.FullName --odir results }

For more complex batches, for example to collect the results in one table, use Python: see Writing case files from Python.

docs.title: Migrating from Forrester
docs.text:
The PyFlange command-line interface replaces the Forrester tool of the Bolt & Beautiful project:

  • forrester determ, sample, inspect and stats become pyflange determ, sample, inspect and stats, with the same options. sample adds the --seed option and writes the same CSV columns.
  • Forrester case files (format version 0.1.0) can be used as they are.
  • forrester hist has been removed: plot the sample CSV with your tool of choice.
  • forrester export-sgre-case is not part of PyFlange: the conversion of company-specific file formats to the PyFlange JSON format is left to dedicated tools.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: If you want to contribute to the PyFlange project, first of all thank you! This document provides guidelines about the most common ways of contributing.

docs.title: Reporting a bug
docs.text:
If you find a bug in PyFlange, you can help by reporting it, so that someone else can fix it. Unless, of course, you know how and want to fix it yourself; in that case see the section Submitting code improvements below.

A bug can be submitted by opening a GitHub issue, but before doing that, please look at the open issues to see if the same bug has already been reported. If so, you can add your contribution to the existing issue.

docs.title: Requesting improvements
docs.text:
If there is a functionality that you would like to see added to PyFlange, please open a GitHub issue, describing the new functionality and explaining why, in your opinion, it is needed. A discussion will follow and eventually someone will be assigned to the implementation of the new functionality.

If you want to implement the new functionality yourself, you can do so by submitting a pull request, but before doing that, please consult the other contributors by opening an issue.

docs.title: Submitting code improvements
docs.text:
Codes modifications and improvements should be submitted via a pull request. Before submitting the pull request, the necessity of the code modification should be discussed in a issue (see Requesting improvements).

Since the typical PyFlange user is expected not to be a professional programmer and probably not familiar with Git, we have created a Git tutorial for non-programmers to make the process of creating a pull request less intimidating.

See also this article about contributing to a project and submitting pull requests.

docs.title: Asking a question
docs.text:
Asking a question is also a form of contribution, equivalent to submitting a bug about the project documentation, which is not complete or not clear. Of course, before submitting a question, make sure you have read the documentation and all the questions submitted by other contributors.

A question can be asked by opening a GitHub issue.

docs.title: Setting up a development environment
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/kcibv/pyflange.git
cd pyflange
py -m pip install -e .
py -m pip install pytest -r docsrc/requirements.txt

The -e option installs PyFlange in editable mode: changes to the source code in src/pyflange are used immediately, without reinstalling.

docs.title: Running the tests and the validation
docs.text:
py -m pytest
py validations/validate.py validations/references/*.json --failed

The tests also run the example scripts of the tutorials (docsrc/examples/*.py). See Validation.

docs.title: Writing documentation
docs.text:
The documentation is written in Markdown in the docsrc folder and built with MkDocs and the Material theme. The API reference is generated from the docstrings by mkdocstrings.

mkdocs serve            # live preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000
mkdocs build --strict   # checks and builds the site into the site folder

(If the mkdocs command is not found, use py -m mkdocs.)

Every change to the code should come with the corresponding documentation change, in the same pull request:

  • Docstrings follow the Google style: a summary line, a description, then Args:, Returns: (or Yields:), Raises: and, where useful, Example: sections. Attributes of dataclasses are documented in an Attributes: section of the class docstring.
  • Docstrings cite the documents of the References page as ref. [n], with the same numbers in every module, followed by the section or equation, e.g. ref. [2], eq. G.36. Each module docstring lists the references it cites in a References: section. A new reference gets the next free number and is added to docsrc/references.md.
  • New public functions or classes appear automatically in the API reference. New modules need a page in docsrc/apis/ and an entry in the nav section of mkdocs.yml.
  • Changes to the command line must be reflected in docsrc/cli.md, changes to the case files in docsrc/json-format.md, and user-visible changes in docsrc/changelog.md.
  • Tutorial code lives in docsrc/examples/*.py and is included in the pages with --8<-- "examples/file.py:section". Update the outputs shown on the pages when the results change, and regenerate the figures with py docsrc/assets/img/make_figures.py. The drawings of the flange geometry are inline SVG files in docsrc/assets/img/*-geometry.svg, styled by docsrc/assets/css/extra.css so that they follow the light and dark themes.

docs.title: Publishing and versions
docs.text:
The site is published on GitHub Pages from the docs folder of the main branch, with one version of the documentation per release (docs/0.13/, docs/0.14/, ...), a latest alias pointing to the newest release, and a dev version for the development branch. The reader chooses the version from the selector next to the site name.

Publishing is automatic: the Documentation GitHub workflow uses mike to build the site and commit it to main:

  • at every push to main, as version major.minor of the version in pyproject.toml (e.g. 0.13 for 0.13.2), moving latest to it;
  • at every push to dev, as version dev.

So, to publish the documentation of a new release, bump the version in pyproject.toml and merge into main. Never edit the docs folder by hand, and do not run mike on a local main branch. To remove an obsolete version, run mike delete --branch main --deploy-prefix docs --push VERSION from a clean clone.

The Tests workflow runs the test suite on Linux and Windows, with the oldest and newest supported Python versions, at every push and pull request to main and dev.

docs.title: PyFlange JSON case format
docs.text:
A fatigue case describes a single-bolt flange segment, its fatigue loads, its bolt S-N curve and, optionally, the statistical parameters needed for a Monte Carlo simulation. PyFlange reads and writes fatigue cases as JSON files in the format described on this page.

The format is used by the command-line interface and by the pyflange.io module:

from pyflange.io import load_fatiguecase, load_fatiguecase_sampler

fcase = load_fatiguecase("case.json")           # deterministic analysis
print(fcase.damage, fcase.fatigue_life)

samp = load_fatiguecase_sampler("case.json")    # random fatigue cases
rnd_fcase = next(samp)

A complete, working example is available here: fatigue-case.json.

Scope: the format currently supports L-flange segments only (PolynomialLFlangeSegment and PolynomialLFlangeSegmentED2). T-flange segments (PolynomialTFlangeSegment) are not supported yet.

docs.title: Format versions
docs.text:
The format version is stored in the top-level format_version field. The current version is 0.2.0.

Version Notes 0.1.0 Original format of the Forrester tool. Files of this version have no format_version field. 0.2.0 Current version. See changes from 0.1.0.

Files of any supported version can be read: files without format_version are assumed to be version 0.1.0 and are converted to the current version on load (see pyflange.io.upgrade_case), so that they keep producing the same results. PyFlange always writes the current version.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Units: all values are in SI units: lengths in m, forces in N, moments in N·m, stresses and elastic moduli in Pa, angles in radians. The only exception is the Markov matrix duration, whose unit is free and determines the unit of the resulting fatigue life (typically years).
  • No hidden defaults: all the parameters marked as required must be given explicitly. In particular, PyFlange does not provide default values for any statistical parameter.
  • Unknown keys are ignored. This allows adding notes or extra data to a case file, and allows reading back the result files written by PyFlange (see Result files), which contain extra report keys.
  • Keys are case-sensitive.

docs.title: Top-level structure
docs.text:
{
    "format_version": "0.2.0",
    "CaseID": "My case",
    "FlangeSegment": { ... },
    "BoltFatigueCurve": { ... },
    "MarkovMatrix": { ... },
    "AllowableDamage": 1.0,
    "SMF": 1.0,
    "Stats": { ... }
}
Key Type Required Description format_version string yes (0.2.0) Format version. If missing, the file is read as version 0.1.0. CaseID any no Case identifier. Not used by PyFlange. FlangeSegment object yes The flange segment. See FlangeSegment. BoltFatigueCurve object yes The bolt S-N curve of the deterministic analysis. See BoltFatigueCurve. MarkovMatrix object yes The flange fatigue loads. See MarkovMatrix. AllowableDamage number no Allowable damage of the deterministic analysis. If omitted, 1.0. SMF number no Stress multiplication factor of the deterministic analysis, applied to the bolt stress ranges. If omitted, 1.0. The command-line option --smf overrides it. Stats object for Monte Carlo only Statistical parameters. See Stats.

docs.title: FlangeSegment
docs.text:
"FlangeSegment": {
    "type": "PolynomialLFlangeSegment",
    "a": 0.150, "b": 0.122, "s": 0.054, "t": 0.172, "R": 4.000,
    "central_angle": 0.0402768,
    "Zg": -115667,
    "bolt": { "type": "StandardMetricBolt", "designation": "M80", "material_grade": "10.9",
              "shank_length": 0.160, "shank_diameter_ratio": "pitch", "stud": true },
    "preload_ratio": 0.75301,
    "Do": 0.086,
    "washer": null,
    "nut": { "type": "RoundNut", "designation": "M80" },
    "gap": { "height": 0.00089, "angle": 0.5236, "shape_factor": 1.0 },
    "tilt_angle": 0.001745,
    "E": 210e9, "G": 80.77e9,
    "s_ratio": 1.0, "r": 0.01,
    "k_shell": "interp",
    "PPL": 0.05, "DFT": 300e-6,
    "settlement_factor": 0.5
}
Key Type Unit Description type string - "PolynomialLFlangeSegment" (IEC 61400-6 AMD1 model) or "PolynomialLFlangeSegmentED2" (IEC 61400-6 ED2 model). Optional, default "PolynomialLFlangeSegment". a number m Distance between the inner face of the flange and the center of the bolt hole. b number m Distance between the center of the bolt hole and the center-line of the shell. s number m Shell thickness. t number m Flange thickness. R number m Shell outer radius. central_angle number rad Angle subtended by the flange segment (2π / number of bolts). Zg number N Shell force per segment at rest (dead weight divided by the number of bolts). Negative if compressive. bolt object - The bolt. See Bolts. preload_ratio number - Bolt preload before losses, as a fraction of the bolt tensile yield force As·fy, where As is the area of the bolt thread cross-section and fy the bolt yield stress. Exactly one of preload_ratio and Fv is required. Fv number N Bolt preload before losses, as absolute value. Exactly one of preload_ratio and Fv is required. Do number m Bolt hole diameter. Standard values are given by pyflange.bolts.standard_hole_diameter. washer object or null - The washer, or null (or omitted) for no washer. See Washers. nut object - The nut. See Nuts. gap object - The flange gap. See Gap. tilt_angle number rad Flange tilt angle. E number Pa Young's modulus of the flange. G number Pa Shear modulus of the flange. s_ratio number - Ratio of the bottom shell thickness over s. r number m Rounding radius between flange and shell. k_shell number, null or "interp" N/m/m Shell stiffness. A number is used as it is; null selects the simplified formula of the model; "interp" interpolates the value from FEA data (see pyflange.flangesegments.shell_stiffness) for the given R, s and gap angle. PPL number - Preload loss due to plastic deformations, as a fraction of Fv (e.g. 0.05 for 5%). DFT number m Dry film thickness of the coatings, used to evaluate the settlement preload losses. settlement_factor number - Factor reducing the settlement preload losses (e.g. 1.0 for torque tightening, 0.5 for tension tightening).

All keys are required, except type, washer and one of preload_ratio / Fv.

docs.title: Bolts
docs.text:
The type key selects one of the following bolt kinds.

StandardMetricBolt: a bolt with standard ISO dimensions and material (see pyflange.bolts.StandardMetricBolt).

Key Type Unit Description designation string - Metric thread designation, e.g. "M80". material_grade string - Material grade, e.g. "10.9". shank_length number m Length of the unthreaded shank. shank_diameter_ratio number or "pitch" - Shank diameter over nominal diameter. "pitch" sets the shank diameter equal to the thread basic pitch diameter (ISO 724), typical of reduced-shank studs. stud boolean - true for stud bolts, false for hexagonal-head bolts.

MetricBolt: a bolt with custom properties (see pyflange.bolts.MetricBolt).

Key Type Unit Description nominal_diameter number m Nominal thread diameter. thread_pitch number m Thread pitch. yield_stress number Pa Yield stress of the bolt material. ultimate_tensile_stress number Pa Ultimate tensile stress of the bolt material. elastic_modulus number Pa Young's modulus of the bolt material. poissons_ratio number - Poisson's ratio of the bolt material. shank_length number m Length of the unthreaded shank. shank_diameter_ratio number - Shank diameter over nominal diameter. stud boolean - true for stud bolts, false for hexagonal-head bolts.

docs.title: Washers
docs.text:
ISOFlatWasher: ISO 7089 flat washer. Key: designation (e.g. "M64").

FlatWasher: custom flat washer (see pyflange.bolts.FlatWasher). Keys: outer_diameter (m), inner_diameter (m), thickness (m), elastic_modulus (Pa), poissons_ratio.

docs.title: Nuts
docs.text:
ISOHexNut: ISO 4032 hexagonal nut. Key: designation.

RoundNut: standard flanged round nut. Key: designation.

HexNut: custom nut (see pyflange.bolts.HexNut). Keys: nominal_diameter (m), thickness (m), inscribed_diameter (m), circumscribed_diameter (m), bearing_diameter (m), elastic_modulus (Pa), poissons_ratio.

docs.title: Gap
docs.text: Key Type Unit Description height number m Maximum gap height. angle number rad Angle subtended by the gap. shape_factor number - Gap shape factor (1.0 for a sinusoidal gap). Optional, default 1.0.

docs.title: BoltFatigueCurve
docs.text:
The S-N curve used in the deterministic analysis. The optional type key selects the curve kind; if omitted, it is "BoltFatigueCurve".

BoltFatigueCurve: IEC 61400-6 AMD1 bolt curve, with slopes 3 and 5, knee point at 2·10⁶ cycles and size effect (see pyflange.fatigue.BoltFatigueCurve).

Key Type Unit Description BoltNominalDiameter number m Bolt nominal diameter, for the size effect. DS_ref number Pa Reference stress range at 2·10⁶ cycles, before size effect and material factor. gamma_M number - Material safety factor.

SingleSlopeFatigueCurve: keys m, DS_ref (Pa), N_ref.

DoubleSlopeFatigueCurve: keys m1, m2, DS_ref (Pa), N_ref, where (DS_ref, N_ref) is the knee point.

In a Monte Carlo simulation, this section is not used: the random S-N curves are defined by Stats.FatigueClassFactor.

docs.title: MarkovMatrix
docs.text:
The fatigue loads, as a list of bins of flange (tower) bending moments.

Key Type Unit Description range list of numbers N·m Bending moment range of each bin. mean list of numbers N·m Mean bending moment of each bin. cycles list of numbers - Number of cycles of each bin. duration number any Duration of the load history (e.g. 30 for 30 years). The fatigue life is given in the same unit.

The three lists must have the same length. Bins with zero range are allowed and give no damage.

docs.title: Stats
docs.text: The Stats section is required only for Monte Carlo simulations. It defines the random variables used to generate random fatigue cases.

docs.title: Distributions
docs.text:
Random variables are described by distribution objects, selected by the Distribution key:

Distribution Keys Description "Normal" Mean, CoV Normal distribution with given mean and coefficient of variation. "LogNormal" Mean, CoV Log-normal distribution with given mean and coefficient of variation. "Weibull" Shape, Scale Weibull distribution. "Beta" Alpha, Beta, x0, x1 Beta distribution defined over [x0, x1]. x0 and x1 are optional (default 0 and 1). "Product" Dist1, Dist2 Product of two independent variables, each described by one of the above distribution objects. Not allowed where a distribution is used as copula marginal.

Mean is expressed in the unit of the variable.

docs.title: Stats keys
docs.text:
"Stats": {
    "Preload":            { "Distribution": "Normal", "MeanRatio": 0.77, "CoV": 0.03 },
    "PlasticLoss":        { "Distribution": "Normal", "Mean": 0.03, "CoV": 0.33333 },
    "DFT":                { "Distribution": "Normal", "Mean": 250e-6, "CoV": 0.12 },
    "Gap":                { "JointDistribution": "IEC 61400-6:2020 AMD1", ... },
    "Tilt":               { "Distribution": "LogNormal", "Mean": 0.001745, "CoV": 0.5 },
    "LoadRangeFactor":    { "Distribution": "LogNormal", "Mean": 1.0, "CoV": 0.12 },
    "FatigueClassFactor": { "Distribution": "Normal", "Mean": 1.0, "CoV": 0.10, "DS_ref_mean": 62e6 },
    "AllowableDamage":    { "Distribution": "LogNormal", "Mean": 1.0, "CoV": 0.30 },
    "StressMultiplicationFactor": { "Distribution": "Product", "Dist1": { ... }, "Dist2": { ... } }
}

All keys are required.

Key Description Preload Bolt preload before losses. Distribution is "Normal" or "LogNormal", with CoV and a mean value given either as MeanRatio (fraction of As·fy, as preload_ratio) or as Mean (N, as Fv). PlasticLoss Preload loss due to plastic deformations, as a fraction of the preload (as PPL). Any distribution. DFT Coating dry film thickness, in m (as DFT). Any distribution. Gap Joint distribution of the gap parameters. See Gap distributions. Tilt Flange tilt angle, in rad. Any distribution. Sampled values are reduced to the interval [0, π]. LoadRangeFactor Factor multiplying all the ranges of the Markov matrix. "LogNormal" only. FatigueClassFactor Factor multiplying the reference stress range of the bolt S-N curve. "Normal" only, with the additional key DS_ref_mean (Pa): the mean reference stress range. Each random curve is a BoltFatigueCurve with DS_ref = DS_ref_mean × factor and gamma_M = 1.0. AllowableDamage Allowable fatigue damage. Any distribution. StressMultiplicationFactor Stress multiplication factor applied to the bolt stress ranges. Any distribution, or a plain number for a constant factor.

docs.title: Gap distributions
docs.text:
The Gap object is selected by the JointDistribution key.

"IEC 61400-6:2020 AMD1": the gap angle is sampled from the Angle distribution; the gap height is then sampled from the AMD1 log-normal distribution for that angle (pyflange.stats.gap_height_distribution) and capped at twice its 95% quantile (see pyflange.stats.standard_gap_sampler).

Key Description FlatnessTolerance Flange flatness tolerance, in m/m (e.g. 0.0014 for 1.4 mm/m). Angle Distribution of the gap angle, in rad. Values outside (0, π) are discarded. ShapeFactor Distribution of the gap shape factor.

"IEC 61400-6:2020 ED2": the gap angle is sampled from the ED2 Beta distribution and the gap height from the ED2 Weibull distribution (see pyflange.stats.standard_gap_sampler_ED2). The shape factor is 1.0.

Key Description FlatnessTolerance Flange flatness tolerance, in m/m.

"ClaytonCopula": gap height and gap angle are correlated via a Clayton copula (see pyflange.stats.clayton_gap_sampler).

Key Description Theta Clayton copula parameter (> 0). Kendall's rank correlation is θ/(θ+2). Height Marginal distribution of the gap height, in m (not "Product"). Angle Marginal distribution of the gap angle, in rad (not "Product"). ShapeFactor Distribution of the gap shape factor.

docs.title: Monte Carlo model
docs.text:
Each random fatigue case is generated as follows (see pyflange.io.create_fatiguecase_sampler and pyflange.stats.standard_PolynomialLFlangeSegment_sampler):

  • The flange segment has the same type and deterministic parameters as FlangeSegment, and random gap and tilt.
  • The shell stiffness is always interpolated from FEA data for the random gap angle: the FlangeSegment.k_shell value is not used.
  • The preload is sampled, reduced by the sampled plastic and settlement losses, and averaged over half of the bolts within the gap (at least one). The resulting segment has PPL = 0 and DFT = 0, because the losses are already included in its preload.
  • The Markov matrix ranges, the S-N curve, the allowable damage and the stress multiplication factor are sampled independently.

The FlangeSegment.PPL, FlangeSegment.DFT, FlangeSegment.gap, FlangeSegment.tilt_angle, FlangeSegment.k_shell, BoltFatigueCurve, AllowableDamage and SMF values are used in deterministic analyses only.

docs.title: Result files
docs.text:
The result files written by pyflange determ and pyflange inspect (and by pyflange.io.fatiguecase_to_dict) use the same format, so they can be loaded back as cases. They contain:

  • format_version, FlangeSegment, BoltFatigueCurve and MarkovMatrix in the current format. The bolt, washer and nut are always written in their explicit forms (MetricBolt, FlatWasher, HexNut), the preload as preload_ratio and k_shell as a number. The BoltFatigueCurve section of a bolt curve also reports the design knee point (m1, m2, DS12, N_ref).
  • damage, allowable_damage, SMF: the analysis results and settings.
  • In verbose mode (always used by the CLI), FatigueLife, the bolt stress Markov matrix BoltStressMarkovMatrix (stresses in Pa) and a report of the flange segment intermediate quantities, added to the FlangeSegment section (BoltPreload, Point1 to Point4, polynomial coefficients, TransferFunctions, stiffnesses, etc.).

docs.title: Changes from version 0.1.0
docs.text:
Version 0.2.0 is a superset of version 0.1.0. The changes are:

  • New format_version field (files without it are read as 0.1.0).
  • FlangeSegment.Fv as an alternative to preload_ratio.
  • FlangeSegment.k_shell accepts "interp".
  • Custom bolts (MetricBolt), washers (FlatWasher) and nuts (HexNut).
  • StandardMetricBolt.shank_diameter_ratio accepts "pitch".
  • Optional BoltFatigueCurve.type, with SingleSlopeFatigueCurve and DoubleSlopeFatigueCurve curves.
  • Optional top-level AllowableDamage and SMF for deterministic analyses.
  • Stats.Preload.Mean as an alternative to MeanRatio.
  • Stats.StressMultiplicationFactor accepts a plain number.
  • Stats.FatigueClassFactor.DS_ref_mean is required. In version 0.1.0 the mean reference stress range of the random S-N curves was implicitly 62 MPa; version 0.1.0 files are upgraded with this value.
  • FlangeSegment.type is optional, with default "PolynomialLFlangeSegment".

Note on Monte Carlo simulations of ED2 cases. The Forrester tool always generated random PolynomialLFlangeSegment (AMD1) segments, even for cases with "type": "PolynomialLFlangeSegmentED2". PyFlange generates random segments of the declared type, so the Monte Carlo results of ED2 cases differ from those computed with Forrester. Deterministic results and AMD1 cases are not affected.

• Units. PyFlange does not convert units. Pass all values in one consistent system, normally SI (m, N, Pa, rad). See Units and conventions.

docs.title: pyflange.bolts
docs.text:
Bolt, washer, and nut fastener components.

This module contains classes and factory functions representing bolt, washer, and nut fastener components. In particular it provides:

  • A MetricBolt class that models generic bolts with metric screw threads and a StandardMetricBolt factory function that generates MetricBolt objects with standard properties.
  • A standard_hole_diameter function returning the standard clearance hole diameter of a metric bolt.
  • A FlatWasher class that models generic flat washers and an ISOFlatWasher factory function that returns a FlatWasher with ISO 7089 standard dimensions.
  • A HexNut class that models generic hexagonal nuts, an ISOHexNut factory function that generates a HexNut with ISO 4032 dimensions, and a RoundNut factory function that generates a standard flanged nut.
  • Bolt, Washer and Nut base classes, and the BoltCrossSection helper class describing a circular cross-section.
Units

All parameters must be supplied in a consistent system of units, e.g. meters for lengths and pascals for stresses.

Example

The following example creates an M80 stud bolt of grade 10.9, together with its standard nut, and evaluates the bolt axial stiffness.

from pyflange.bolts import StandardMetricBolt, RoundNut

bolt = StandardMetricBolt("M80", "10.9", shank_length=0.160, stud=True)
nut = RoundNut("M80")
k = bolt.axial_stiffness(0.35)    # axial stiffness for a 350 mm clamped length
References

The reference numbers are the same in all the PyFlange modules (see the references page). This module cites:

  • [2] IEC 61400-6:2020+AMD1:2025 CSV. Wind energy generation systems - Part 6: Tower and foundation design requirements. Consolidated version,
  • The bolt tensile resistance is given by its eq. G.6.

and the following product and design standards:

  • ISO 68-1:1998, ISO general purpose screw threads - Basic profile.
  • ISO 724, ISO general-purpose metric screw threads - Basic dimensions.
  • ISO 898-1:2013, Mechanical properties of fasteners - Part 1: Bolts, screws and studs.
  • ISO 4032, Hexagon regular nuts (style 1).
  • ISO 7089, Plain washers - Normal series.
  • EN 1993-1-8:2005, Eurocode 3 - Design of joints.
  • VDI 2230 Part 1, Systematic calculation of highly stressed bolted joints.

Classes:

  • Bolt –

    Base class for bolt representations.

  • BoltCrossSection –

    Circular cross-section of a bolt.

  • MetricBolt –

    Generic bolt with ISO 68-1 metric screw thread.

  • Washer –

    Base class for washer representations.

  • FlatWasher –

    Generic flat washer.

  • Nut –

    Base class for nut representations.

  • HexNut –

    Generic hexagonal nut.

Functions:

  • StandardMetricBolt –

    Create a metric bolt with standard dimensions and material properties.

  • standard_hole_diameter –

    Return the standard clearance hole diameter for a metric bolt.

  • ISOFlatWasher –

    Generate a standard flat washer according to ISO 7089.

  • ISOHexNut –

    Generate a standard hexagonal nut according to ISO 4032.

  • RoundNut –

    Generate a standard flanged round nut.

MetricBolt(nominal_diameter, thread_pitch, yield_stress, ultimate_tensile_stress, elastic_modulus=210 * GPa, poissons_ratio=0.3, shank_length=0, shank_diameter_ratio=1, stud=False)

Bases: Bolt

Generic bolt with ISO 68-1 metric screw thread.

The parameters must be expressed in a consistent system of units. For example, if you choose to input distances in meters (m) and forces in newtons (N), then stresses must be expressed in pascals (N/m²). All bolt attributes and methods return values consistent with the input units of measurement.

All input parameters are also available as attributes of the generated instance (e.g. bolt.shank_length, bolt.yield_stress, etc.).

Instances of this class are designed to be immutable; changing attributes after instantiation is not recommended. If a bolt with different parameters is needed, instantiate a new one.

Attributes:

  • nominal_diameter (float) –

    Outermost (nominal) diameter of the screw thread.

  • thread_pitch (float) –

    Pitch of the metric thread.

  • yield_stress (float) –

    Nominal yield stress (0.2% strain limit) of the bolt material.

  • ultimate_tensile_stress (float) –

    Nominal ultimate tensile stress of the bolt material.

  • elastic_modulus (float) –

    Young's modulus of the bolt material. Defaults to 210 GPa (210e9 N/m²).

  • poissons_ratio (float) –

    Poisson's ratio of the bolt material. Defaults to 0.3.

  • shank_length (float) –

    Length of the unthreaded shank. Defaults to 0.0.

  • shank_diameter_ratio (float) –

    Ratio between the shank diameter and the nominal diameter. Defaults to 1.0 (shank has nominal diameter).

  • stud (bool) –

    True if this is a stud bolt, False otherwise. Defaults to False.

Methods:

  • ultimate_tensile_capacity –

    Evaluate the ultimate tensile force that the bolt can sustain.

  • axial_stiffness –

    Evaluate the axial stiffness of the clamped bolt.

  • bending_stiffness –

    Evaluate the bending stiffness of the clamped bolt.

docs.title: ultimate_tensile_capacity
docs.text:
ultimate_tensile_capacity(standard='Eurocode')

Evaluate the ultimate tensile force that the bolt can sustain.

According to EN 1993-1-8, the tensile resistance is 0.9 * fub * As / 1.25, where fub is the ultimate tensile stress and As the area of thread_cross_section. This is also the tensile resistance F_t,R used by the flange segment models (ref. [2], eq. G.6).

Parameters:

  • standard (str, default: 'Eurocode' ) –

    Standard according to which the ultimate tensile force should be calculated. Currently supported: "Eurocode" (EN 1993-1-8:2005). Defaults to "Eurocode".

Returns:

  • float –

    The bolt ultimate tensile force according to the specified standard.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If the requested standard is not supported.

docs.title: StandardMetricBolt
docs.text:
StandardMetricBolt(designation, material_grade, shank_length=0.0, shank_diameter_ratio=1.0, stud=False)

Create a metric bolt with standard dimensions and material properties.

This function provides a convenient way of creating a MetricBolt object, given the standard geometry designation (e.g. "M20") and the standard material grade designation (e.g. "8.8").

Parameters:

  • designation (str) –

    Metric screw thread designation. Allowed values: 'M4', 'M5', 'M6', 'M8', 'M10', 'M12', 'M14', 'M16', 'M18', 'M20', 'M22', 'M24', 'M27', 'M30', 'M33', 'M36', 'M39', 'M42', 'M45', 'M48', 'M52', 'M56', 'M60', 'M64', 'M72', 'M80', 'M90', 'M100'.

  • material_grade (str) –

    Material grade designation. Allowed values: - Carbon-steel: '4.6', '4.8', '5.6', '5.8', '6.8', '8.8', '9.8', '10.9', '12.9' - Austenitic stainless: 'A50', 'A70', 'A80', 'A100' - Duplex stainless: 'D70', 'D80', 'D100' - Martensitic stainless: 'C50', 'C70', 'C80', 'C110' - Ferritic stainless: 'F45', 'F60'

  • shank_length (float, default: 0.0 ) –

    Length of the unthreaded shank. Defaults to 0.0.

  • shank_diameter_ratio (float | str, default: 1.0 ) –

    Ratio between the shank diameter and the bolt nominal diameter. If it is the string "pitch", the shank diameter is taken equal to the thread basic pitch diameter (ISO 724), as is common for reduced-shank stud bolts. Defaults to 1.0.

  • stud (bool, default: False ) –

    True if this is a stud bolt, False otherwise. Defaults to False.

Returns:

  • MetricBolt –

    A MetricBolt instance with standard properties.

Example 
# M80 stud bolt whose shank diameter equals the thread pitch diameter
bolt = StandardMetricBolt("M80", "10.9", shank_length=0.160,
                          shank_diameter_ratio="pitch", stud=True)

PyFlange command-line interface.

The command-line interface performs deterministic and probabilistic (Monte Carlo) bolt fatigue analyses of flange cases described in the PyFlange JSON format (see pyflange.io). It can be invoked as pyflange or as python -m pyflange, followed by one of these commands:

docs.title: pyflange.fatigue
docs.text:
Fatigue calculation and S-N curve tools for flanged connections.

This module provides data structures, fatigue (Wöhler) curve representations, and analysis classes to evaluate structural fatigue damage and fatigue life for large bolted flanges.

Key components provided by this module:

  • MarkovMatrix: Encapsulates a discrete cyclic load or stress history (load ranges, mean values, cycle counts, and duration) obtained from rainflow counting or design load spectra.
  • FatigueCurve: Abstract base class defining the S-N curve interface and Palmgren-Miner linear cumulative damage accumulation \(D = \sum_{i} n_i / N(\Delta S_i)\).
  • SingleSlopeFatigueCurve: Represents a Wöhler curve with a single logarithmic slope exponent \(m\), defined by the power law \(N \cdot \Delta S^m = a\).
  • MultiSlopeFatigueCurve: Represents a composite multi-slope S-N curve constructed as the upper envelope of multiple single-slope curve segments.
  • DoubleSlopeFatigueCurve: Represents a bilinear S-N curve with two slopes (\(m_1, m_2\)) intersecting at a transition knee point \((\Delta S_{12}, N_{12})\).
  • BoltFatigueCurve: Specialized bilinear S-N curve for threaded bolts conforming to IEC 61400-6 AMD1, incorporating nominal diameter size-effect corrections and a material partial safety factor \(\gamma_M\).
  • BoltFatigueAnalysis: End-to-end fatigue analysis pipeline that evaluates bolt stress spectra from flange bending moment histories, calculates total cumulative damage, and predicts bolt fatigue life.
Units

All parameters must be supplied in a consistent system of units. When using SI units:

  • Distances and diameters: meters (m)
  • Forces: newtons (N)
  • Bending moments: newton-meters (N·m)
  • Stresses and pressures: pascals (Pa)
  • Duration and fatigue life: consistent time units (e.g., seconds or years)
References

The reference numbers are the same in all the PyFlange modules (see the references page). This module cites:

  • [1] Seidel, M.: IEC 61400-6 AMD1 Background document. Fatigue design for ring flange connections in wind turbine support structures. Rev00, Siemens Gamesa, 2024. Section 3 explains the selection of the bolt S-N curve.
  • [2] IEC 61400-6:2020+AMD1:2025 CSV. Wind energy generation systems - Part 6: Tower and foundation design requirements. Consolidated version,
  • The bolt damage calculation is given in section 6.7.5.4.
  • [5] Seidel, M.: IEC 61400-6 AMD1 & ED2 Background document. Rev01, draft 2026-08-04, Siemens Gamesa. Section 3 explains the selection of the bolt S-N curve.

Classes:

  • MarkovMatrix –

    A Markov matrix representation of a cyclic load history.

  • FatigueCurve –

    Abstract base class for Wöhler (S-N) fatigue strength curves.

  • SingleSlopeFatigueCurve –

    Wöhler (S-N) fatigue curve with a single logarithmic slope.

  • MultiSlopeFatigueCurve –

    Multi-slope composite Wöhler (S-N) fatigue curve.

  • DoubleSlopeFatigueCurve –

    Bilinear (double-slope) Wöhler (S-N) fatigue curve.

  • BoltFatigueCurve –

    Bolt fatigue S-N curve according to IEC 61400-6 AMD1.

  • BoltFatigueAnalysis –

    Fatigue analysis pipeline for a flange bolt.

A Markov matrix representation of a cyclic load history.

Encapsulates a discrete load or stress spectrum resulting from cycle counting (e.g., rainflow counting). The load history is characterized by arrays of cycle ranges, mean values, and associated cycle counts, along with an overall duration.

The physical quantity represented can be stress (Pa), force (N), bending moment (N·m), etc., provided that consistent units are maintained throughout downstream calculations.

    Array containing the number of applied cycles (\(n\)) for each (range, mean) bin.

  • duration (float) –

    Time duration represented by the load history (e.g., in seconds or years). Defaults to 1.0.

docs.title: FatigueCurve
docs.text:
Abstract base class for Wöhler (S-N) fatigue strength curves.

This class provides the interface for evaluating fatigue endurance (number of cycles to failure \(N\) as a function of stress range \(\Delta S\), and vice versa), as well as calculating fatigue damage and cumulative damage using the Palmgren-Miner linear cumulative damage hypothesis:

\[D = \sum_{i} \frac{n_i}{N(\Delta S_i)}\]

This class should not be instantiated directly; use one of its concrete subclasses such as SingleSlopeFatigueCurve, DoubleSlopeFatigueCurve, or BoltFatigueCurve.

    Calculates the number of cycles to failure for a given stress range.

  • DS –

    Calculates the allowable stress range for a given number of cycles.

  • damage –

    Calculates fatigue damage according to the Palmgren-Miner rule.

  • cumulated_damage –

    Calculates cumulative fatigue damage according to Miner's sum.

cumulated_damage(markov_matrix)

Calculates cumulative fatigue damage according to Miner's sum.

Evaluates the total cumulative damage over all bins in the load spectrum:

\[D_{\text{total}} = \sum_{i} \frac{n_i}{N(\Delta S_i)}\]

Bins producing NaN damage values (e.g., zero stress or invalid evaluations) are ignored in the summation via numpy.nansum.

    Total cumulative fatigue damage index \(D_{\text{total}}\).

SingleSlopeFatigueCurve(m, DS_ref, N_ref)

Bases: FatigueCurve

Wöhler (S-N) fatigue curve with a single logarithmic slope.

Represents a linear S-N relationship in log-log space governed by the power-law equation:

\[N \cdot \Delta S^m = a = \Delta S_{\text{ref}}^m \cdot N_{\text{ref}}\]

where \(m\) is the inverse slope exponent, \(\Delta S_{\text{ref}}\) is a reference stress range, and \(N_{\text{ref}}\) is the corresponding cycle count at failure.

    Negative inverse slope of the S-N curve in log-log coordinates (\(-\frac{\mathrm{d}\log N}{\mathrm{d}\log \Delta S}\)).

  • DS_ref (float) –

    Reference stress range \(\Delta S_{\text{ref}}\) (e.g., in Pa).

  • N_ref (float) –

    Reference number of cycles to failure \(N_{\text{ref}}\) at stress range DS_ref.

Methods:

  • N –

    Calculates the number of cycles to failure for given stress range(s).

  • DS –

    Calculates the allowable stress range for given cycle count(s).

DoubleSlopeFatigueCurve(m1, m2, DS12, N12)

Bases: MultiSlopeFatigueCurve

Bilinear (double-slope) Wöhler (S-N) fatigue curve.

Implements a two-slope S-N curve commonly used in structural design standards (e.g., Eurocode 3, DNV, IEC standards). The curve transitions from slope \(m_1\) in the lower-cycle / higher-stress regime (\(N \le N_{12}\)) to slope \(m_2\) in the higher-cycle / lower-stress regime (\(N > N_{12}\)) at an intersection knee point \((\Delta S_{12}, N_{12})\).

Parameters:

    Logarithmic slope exponent for the lower-cycle regime (\(N \le N_{12}\)).

  • m2 (float) –

    Logarithmic slope exponent for the higher-cycle regime (\(N > N_{12}\)).

  • DS12 (float) –

    Stress range \(\Delta S_{12}\) at the knee point where the two slopes meet.

  • N12 (float) –

    Number of cycles \(N_{12}\) at the knee point where the two slopes meet.

Initializes the DoubleSlopeFatigueCurve (see the class documentation).

docs.title: BoltFatigueCurve
docs.text:
BoltFatigueCurve(diameter, DS_ref=50000000.0, gamma_M=1.1)

Bases: DoubleSlopeFatigueCurve

Bolt fatigue S-N curve according to IEC 61400-6 AMD1.

Constructs a design bilinear S-N curve for threaded bolts with logarithmic slopes \(m_1 = 3\) (for \(N \le 2 \times 10^6\)) and \(m_2 = 5\) (for \(N > 2 \times 10^6\)), with a knee point located at \(N_{12} = 2 \times 10^6\) cycles (ref. [2], section 6.7.5.4).

The characteristic reference stress range \(\Delta \sigma_c\) at 2 million cycles is adjusted for bolt size effects with the factor \(k_s\) of ref. [2], eq. (44):

  • For \(d \le 30\text{ mm}\): \(\Delta \sigma_c = \Delta S_{\text{ref}}\)
  • For \(30\text{ mm} < d \le 72\text{ mm}\): \(\Delta \sigma_c = \Delta S_{\text{ref}} \cdot \left(\frac{0.030}{d}\right)^{0.1}\)
  • For \(d > 72\text{ mm}\): \(\Delta \sigma_c = \Delta S_{\text{ref}} \cdot \left(\frac{0.030}{d}\right)^{0.1} \cdot \left(\frac{0.072}{d}\right)^{0.25}\)

The knee point stress range for the design curve is obtained by dividing the characteristic strength by the material partial safety factor:

\[\Delta S_{12} = \frac{\Delta \sigma_c}{\gamma_M}\]

The curve has no endurance limit. With the default parameters (detail category 50, \(\gamma_M = 1.1\)) it is the design curve of ref. [2], section 6.7.5.4. In Monte Carlo simulations, random curves are generated with \(\gamma_M = 1.0\) and a random \(\Delta S_{\text{ref}}\) (see pyflange.stats.standard_bolt_fatigue_curve_sampler).

Parameters:

  • diameter (float) –

    Nominal bolt diameter \(d\) in meters.

  • DS_ref (float, default: 50000000.0 ) –

    Reference characteristic stress range \(\Delta S_{\text{ref}}\) at \(2 \times 10^6\) cycles before size and material factor corrections (in Pa). Defaults to 50 MPa (50e6 Pa), i.e. detail category 50 of ref. [2].

  • gamma_M (float, default: 1.1 ) –

    Material partial safety factor \(\gamma_M\) for fatigue design. Defaults to 1.1 (ref. [2], section 6.7.5.4).

Attributes:

  • diameter (float) –

    The nominal bolt diameter passed to the constructor.

  • DS_ref (float) –

    The reference stress range passed to the constructor.

  • gamma_M (float) –

    The material safety factor passed to the constructor.

Example 
import numpy as np
from pyflange.fatigue import BoltFatigueCurve, MarkovMatrix

curve = BoltFatigueCurve(0.080)       # M80 bolt, default fatigue class
N = curve.N(40e6)                     # cycles to failure at a 40 MPa range

mkvm = MarkovMatrix(range=np.array([20e6, 40e6]),
                    mean=np.array([300e6, 300e6]),
                    cycles=np.array([1e6, 1e4]),
                    duration=20)      # e.g. 20 years
D = curve.cumulated_damage(mkvm)      # Miner's sum

Initializes the BoltFatigueCurve (see the class documentation).

docs.title: BoltFatigueAnalysis dataclass
docs.text:
BoltFatigueAnalysis(fseg, flange_mkvm, custom_fatigue_curve=None, allowable_damage=1.0, SMF=1.0)

Fatigue analysis pipeline for a flange bolt.

Evaluates the cyclic stress history, total cumulative fatigue damage, and expected fatigue life for a bolt in a flanged connection under external bending moment histories.

The analysis transforms the flange shell moment Markov matrix into a bolt stress Markov matrix using the segment's non-linear transfer functions, accounting for axial force, bolt bending, bolt diameter effects, and dynamic stress multiplication. The bolt stress range is the axial stress range plus the bending stress range reduced by the factor \(\kappa_b\) (ref. [2], eqs. (42) and (43)), and the damage is evaluated with Miner's rule (ref. [2], section 6.7.5.4).

Attributes:

  • fseg (FlangeSegment) –

    The flange segment model containing geometry, bolt properties, preloads, and transfer functions.

  • flange_mkvm (MarkovMatrix) –

    The Markov matrix representing the external bending moment load history acting on the flange connection.

  • custom_fatigue_curve (FatigueCurve | None) –

    Optional custom S-N curve for the bolt. If None, an IEC 61400-6 AMD1 compliant BoltFatigueCurve is automatically constructed from the bolt nominal diameter. Defaults to None.

  • allowable_damage (float) –

    Maximum allowable cumulative fatigue damage limit \(D_{\text{allow}}\). Defaults to 1.0 (ref. [2], section 6.7.5.4).

  • SMF (float) –

    Stress Multiplication Factor applied to the bolt stress ranges to account for the model uncertainty of the analytical model (ref. [5], section 6.5). Defaults to 1.0.

Example 
import numpy as np
from pyflange.fatigue import MarkovMatrix, BoltFatigueAnalysis

# fseg is a flange segment, e.g. a PolynomialLFlangeSegment
mkvm = MarkovMatrix(range=np.array([20e6, 40e6]),     # N·m
                    mean=np.array([30e6, 30e6]),      # N·m
                    cycles=np.array([1e7, 1e5]),
                    duration=25)                      # years
analysis = BoltFatigueAnalysis(fseg, mkvm)
print(analysis.damage, analysis.fatigue_life)

docs.title: pyflange.flangesegments
docs.text:
Mechanical models of single-bolt flange segments.

This module contains FlangeSegment classes, which model the mechanical behavior of a flange sector containing one bolt only. The module provides:

  • Gap: description of the imperfection gap between two flange faces.
  • FlangeSegment: abstract base class defining the transfer-function interface (bolt axial force and bolt bending moment as functions of the shell pull force).
  • PolynomialFlangeSegment: abstract base class implementing the polynomial transfer functions of refs. [1] and [2].
  • PolynomialLFlangeSegment and PolynomialLFlangeSegmentED2: polynomial L-flange segment models (the latter implementing the modifications expected in IEC 61400-6 ED2).
  • PolynomialTFlangeSegment and PolynomialTFlangeSegmentED2: polynomial T-flange segment models (the latter implementing the modifications expected in IEC 61400-6 ED2).
  • bolt_markov_matrix: conversion of a flange bending-moment Markov matrix into a bolt stress Markov matrix, via the segment transfer functions.
  • shell_stiffness: shell stiffness interpolated from tabulated FEA results.

The only types of FlangeSegment currently available are an L-Flange segment and a T-Flange segment, implementing a polynomial relation between tower shell force and bolt force / bolt moment. Nonetheless, this module has been structured to be easily extensible with other types of FlangeSegment model, such as Multilinear (Petersen) L-Flanges, Multilinear T-Flanges, etc.

Units

All parameters must be supplied in a consistent system of units, e.g. meters for lengths, newtons for forces and pascals for stresses. Angles are expressed in radians.

Example

The following example creates an L-flange segment and evaluates the bolt axial force for a given shell pull force.

from math import pi
from pyflange.bolts import StandardMetricBolt, RoundNut
from pyflange.flangesegments import Gap, PolynomialLFlangeSegment

fseg = PolynomialLFlangeSegment(
    a=0.150, b=0.122, s=0.054, t=0.172, R=4.0,
    central_angle=2*pi/156,
    Zg=-115e3,                              # dead weight per bolt (compression)
    bolt=StandardMetricBolt("M80", "10.9", shank_length=0.160, stud=True),
    Fv=2.9e6,                               # bolt preload
    Do=0.086, washer=None, nut=RoundNut("M80"),
    gap=Gap(height=0.002, angle=pi/6))

Fs = fseg.bolt_axial_force(500e3)           # bolt force for a shell pull of 500 kN
References

The reference numbers are the same in all the PyFlange modules (see the references page). This module cites:

  • [1] Seidel, M.: IEC 61400-6 AMD1 Background document. Fatigue design for ring flange connections in wind turbine support structures. Rev00, Siemens Gamesa, 2024.
  • [2] IEC 61400-6:2020+AMD1:2025 CSV. Wind energy generation systems - Part 6: Tower and foundation design requirements. Consolidated version,
  • Equation numbers G.xx refer to its Annex G.
  • [3] Petersen, C.: Nachweis der Betriebsfestigkeit exzentrisch beanspruchter Ringflanschverbindungen. Stahlbau 67 (1998), pp. 191-203. https://doi.org/10.1002/stab.199800690
  • [4] Petersen, C.: Stahlbau. 4th edition, Springer Vieweg, 2012. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-8348-8610-1
  • [5] Seidel, M.: IEC 61400-6 AMD1 & ED2 Background document. Fatigue design for ring flange connections in wind turbine support structures. Rev01, draft 2026-08-04, Siemens Gamesa. The changes of the polynomial model from AMD1 to ED2 are summarised in its section 9.7.
  • [6] Tobinaga, I.; Ishihara, T.: A study of action point correction factor for L-type flanges of wind turbine towers. Wind Energy 21 (2018), pp. 801-806. https://doi.org/10.1002/we.2193

docs.text:
Bases: FlangeSegment

A generic FlangeSegment with polynomial transfer functions.

This class implements a polynomial relation between tower shell force Z and bolt axial force Fs or bolt bending moment Ms. It is not meant to be instantiated directly but to be subclassed.

The polynomial transfer functions are defined by 4 reference points:

  • P1: Flange segment at rest.
  • P2: Flange segment at ultimate tensile limit state.
  • P3: Flange segment in small tensile deformation.
  • P4: Gap closure state.

Child classes must provide the coordinates of these points (shell force, bolt force and bolt moment) through the abstract properties of this class. The transfer functions are a quadratic polynomial through P1, P2 and P3 in the tensile domain (above the shell force at rest), a quadratic polynomial between P4 and P1 in the compressive domain, and a constant below P4. Child classes may override the tensile polynomials when the reference defines them differently (e.g. the cubic bolt moment of T-flanges).

    Calculates bolt axial force from tower shell force using a polynomial.

  • bolt_bending_moment –

docs.title: bolt_markov_matrix
docs.text:
bolt_markov_matrix(fseg, flange_markov_matrix, bending_factor=0.0, macro_geometric_factor=1.0, mean_factor=1.0, range_factor=1.0, SMF=1.0)

Evaluates the bolt Markov matrix from the shell Markov matrix.

The flange bending moment ranges and means are converted into shell pull forces acting on the flange segment, and then into minimum and maximum bolt stresses through the transfer functions of the flange segment. The bolt stress is the sum of the axial stress and of the bending stress scaled by bending_factor, evaluated on the bolt thread cross-section, according to ref. [2], section 6.7.5.4, eq. (42).

The flange bending moment M is converted into the segment shell force as Z = M / W * A_seg (ref. [2], eq. G.33), where W is the section modulus of the tower shell, evaluated at the shell mid-surface, and A_seg the shell cross-section area of the segment.

Parameters:

  • fseg (PolynomialFlangeSegment) –

    The flange segment containing the transfer functions. WARNING: Currently only works with PolynomialFlangeSegments.

  • flange_markov_matrix (MarkovMatrix) –

    The Markov matrix of bending moments on the flange.

  • bending_factor (float, default: 0.0 ) –

    Factor for the bending portion of the total stress range (kappa_b of ref. [2], eq. (43)). Defaults to 0.0 (axial stress only).

  • macro_geometric_factor (float, default: 1.0 ) –

    Factor for macro geometric influences (the SCF of ref. [2], section 6.7.5.3), affecting dead weight, mean, and range values. If omitted, it defaults to 1.0.

  • mean_factor (float, default: 1.0 ) –

    Factor for the mean values of the tower's bending moments. If omitted, it defaults to 1.0.

  • range_factor (float, default: 1.0 ) –

    Factor for the range of the tower's bending moments. If omitted, it defaults to 1.0.

  • SMF (float, default: 1.0 ) –

    Stress Multiplication Factor to be applied to bolt Markov matrix stress ranges. If omitted, it defaults to 1.0.

Returns:

  • MarkovMatrix –

    The bolt's Markov matrix representing the stress history. Its cycles and duration are the same as the flange Markov matrix.

docs.text:
shell_stiffness(shell_radius, shell_thickness, gap_angle)

Calculates the axial stiffness of a flange-segment shell via interpolation.

This function interpolates shell stiffness from a dataset of 2160 FEA results, covering 8 diameters (3 m to 10 m), 15 shell thicknesses (10 mm to 150 mm) and 18 gap angles (10° to 180°). This is the database of pre-computed stiffness values described in ref. [5], section 9.3.1, as an alternative to the simplified formula of ref. [2], eqs. G.43 and G.44. Values outside the range covered by the dataset are not extrapolated, and nan is returned instead.

Example 
from math import pi
from pyflange.flangesegments import shell_stiffness

k_shell = shell_stiffness(4.0, 0.054, pi/6)   # R = 4 m, s = 54 mm, 30° gap

Parameters:

  • shell_radius (float) –

    Outer radius of the shell.

  • shell_thickness (float) –

    Thickness of the shell.

  • gap_angle (float) –

    Angular length of the flange gap in radians.

Returns:

  • float –

    The interpolated shell stiffness (K_sh), or nan if the arguments are outside the dataset range.

docs.text:
Reading and writing flange fatigue cases in the PyFlange JSON format.

This module implements the PyFlange JSON case format, documented in detail in the JSON format reference. In particular it provides:

  • Loaders, that convert a JSON case file (or the equivalent dictionary) into PyFlange objects: load_fatiguecase, load_fatiguecase_sampler and the lower-level create_* functions.
  • Exporters, that convert PyFlange objects back into dictionaries in the same format (*_to_dict functions) and write dictionaries to JSON or Excel files (dict_to_json, dict_to_excel).
  • Monte Carlo helpers: sample_fatiguecase, that runs a simulation and returns a table of realizations, and create_realization, that rebuilds a single realization from that table.
Format versions

The current format version is 0.2.0 (FORMAT_VERSION). Files without a format_version field are assumed to be version 0.1.0 (the format used by the former Forrester tool) and are upgraded on the fly by upgrade_case, so they keep producing the same results.

Units

All values are expressed in SI units (m, N, Pa, rad), except where stated otherwise in the format reference.

Example 
from pyflange.io import load_fatiguecase, fatiguecase_to_dict, dict_to_json

fcase = load_fatiguecase("case.json")       # a BoltFatigueAnalysis object
print(fcase.damage, fcase.fatigue_life)

dict_to_json(fatiguecase_to_dict(fcase, verbose=True), "case-res.json")

docs.title: pyflange.stats
docs.text:
Probability distributions and random samplers for probabilistic flange analyses.

This module contains tools for the probabilistic analysis of flanged connections. In particular, two categories of tools are provided:

  • Probability distributions for some flange properties.
  • Samplers: random realization generators for flange properties.

The provided probability distributions are:

  • gap_height_distribution (IEC 61400-6 AMD1)
  • gap_height_distribution_ED2 and gap_angle_distribution_ED2 (IEC 61400-6 ED2)

The samplers are just Python generator functions that yield random values. Samplers can be used in a loop or to generate random values via the python next function. The following general-purpose samplers are available:

  • sampler
  • norm_sampler
  • lognorm_sampler
  • weibull_sampler
  • beta_sampler
  • product_sampler
  • clayton_copula_sampler
  • clayton_gap_sampler
  • fatigue_case_sampler

The following samplers implement the stochastic model of the IEC 61400-6 background documents (refs. [1] and [5]):

  • standard_gap_sampler
  • standard_gap_sampler_ED2
  • standard_PolynomialLFlangeSegment_sampler
  • standard_markov_matrix_sampler
  • standard_bolt_fatigue_curve_sampler

An example of how to use the above generators to perform a Monte Carlo simulation is given in the Monte Carlo in Python tutorial.

Random values are drawn from the numpy global random generator, so a simulation can be made reproducible with numpy.random.seed.

References

The reference numbers are the same in all the PyFlange modules (see the references page). This module cites:

  • [1] Seidel, M.: IEC 61400-6 AMD1 Background document. Fatigue design for ring flange connections in wind turbine support structures. Rev00, Siemens Gamesa, 2024. The stochastic model is given in its Table 7.
  • [2] IEC 61400-6:2020+AMD1:2025 CSV. Wind energy generation systems - Part 6: Tower and foundation design requirements. Consolidated version,
  • The design gap height is defined in section 6.7.5.2.
  • [5] Seidel, M.: IEC 61400-6 AMD1 & ED2 Background document. Rev01, draft 2026-08-04, Siemens Gamesa. The ED2 gap heights are given in section 2.2.4 and the stochastic model in section 6.4 (Table 8).

Functions:

  • gap_height_distribution –

    Evaluates the gap height probability distribution according to IEC 61400-6 AMD1.

  • gap_height_distribution_ED2 –

    Evaluates the gap height probability distribution proposed for IEC 61400-6 ED2.

  • gap_angle_distribution_ED2 –

    Evaluates the gap angle probability distribution used for ED2 Monte Carlo simulations.

  • sampler –

    Generic distribution-based sampler.

  • norm_sampler –

    Sampler based on a Normal distribution.

  • lognorm_sampler –

    Sampler based on a Log-Normal distribution.

  • weibull_sampler –

    Sampler based on a Weibull distribution.

  • beta_sampler –

    Sampler based on a Beta distribution.

  • standard_gap_sampler –

    Sampler that generates random flange gaps according to IEC 61400-6 AMD1.

  • standard_gap_sampler_ED2 –

    Sampler that generates random flange gaps for IEC 61400-6 ED2.

  • product_sampler –

    Sampler of the product of two independent random variables.

  • clayton_copula_sampler –

    Sampler of two random variables joined by a Clayton copula.

  • clayton_gap_sampler –

    Sampler that generates random flange gaps with correlated height and angle.

  • standard_PolynomialLFlangeSegment_sampler –

    A sampler that yields random pyflange PolynomialLFlangeSegment objects.

  • standard_markov_matrix_sampler –

    Sampler that generates a random Markov matrix.

  • standard_bolt_fatigue_curve_sampler –

    Sampler that generates random bolt S-N curves.

  • fatigue_case_sampler –

    Sampler that generates random fatigue cases.

docs.title: gap_height_distribution
docs.text:
gap_height_distribution(flange_diameter, flange_flatness_tolerance, gap_length)

Evaluates the gap height probability distribution according to IEC 61400-6 AMD1.

The gap height is modeled as a log-normal random variable, whose mean value and coefficient of variation depend on the flange diameter, the flatness tolerance and the gap length (ref. [2], section 6.7.5.2, eqs. (32) to (38)). The design gap height is the 95% quantile of this distribution (ref. [2], eqs. (39) and (40)). The formulae may be used for flange diameters up to 10 m.

Parameters:

  • flange_diameter (float) –

    The outer diameter of the flange, expressed in meters.

  • flange_flatness_tolerance (float) –

    The local flatness tolerance u_tol,1m of ref. [2], expressed in mm/mm (non-dimensional, e.g. 0.0014 for 1.4 mm/m).

  • gap_length (float) –

    The length of the gap, expressed in meters and measured at the outer edge of the flange.

Returns:

  • rv_frozen –

    A frozen SciPy log-normal distribution (scipy.stats.lognorm) representing the gap height stochastic variable, expressed in meters.

Example

The following example creates a gap distribution and then calculates the 95% quantile of the gap height.

from pyflange.stats import gap_height_distribution

D = 7.50      # Flange diameter in meters
u = 0.0014    # Flatness tolerance (non-dimensional)
L = 1.22      # Gap length
gap_dist = gap_height_distribution(D, u, L)     # a lognorm distribution object

u95 = gap_dist.ppf(0.95)    # PPF is the inverse of CDF. See scipy.stats.lognorm documentation.

docs.title: gap_height_distribution_ED2
docs.text:
gap_height_distribution_ED2(flange_diameter, flange_flatness_tolerance, gap_length)

Evaluates the gap height probability distribution proposed for IEC 61400-6 ED2.

The gap height is modeled as a Weibull random variable, whose shape and scale parameters depend on the flange diameter, the flatness tolerance and the gap angle (ref. [5], section 2.2.4, eqs. (25) to (28)). The ED2 design gap height is the 75% quantile of this distribution (ref. [5], eq. (24)).

Parameters:

  • flange_diameter (float) –

    The outer diameter of the flange, in meters.

  • flange_flatness_tolerance (float) –

    The flatness tolerance, in mm/mm (non-dimensional).

  • gap_length (float) –

    The length of the gap, in meters, measured at the outer edge of the flange.

Returns:

  • rv_frozen –

    A frozen SciPy Weibull distribution (scipy.stats.weibull_min) representing the gap height, in meters.

Example 
from math import pi
from pyflange.stats import gap_height_distribution_ED2

D = 7.50                         # Flange diameter in meters
u = 0.0014                       # Flatness tolerance (1.4 mm/m)
L = pi/6 * D/2                   # Length of a 30 deg gap
dist = gap_height_distribution_ED2(D, u, L)
k_design = dist.ppf(0.75)        # ED2 design gap height (75% quantile)

The gap angle is modeled as a Beta random variable defined over the interval [0, pi], whose parameters depend on the flange diameter and flatness tolerance. This distribution is used together with gap_height_distribution_ED2. Note that it is not given in refs. [2] and [5].

docs.title: sampler
docs.text:
sampler(random_variable)

Generic distribution-based sampler.

Parameters:

  • random_variable (rv_continuous) –

    Any SciPy continuous random variable.

Yields:

  • float –

    A random realization of the passed random variable, at every next call.

Example

The following example creates a Normal distribution sampler and generates three realizations.

from scipy.stats import norm
ndist = norm(12.0, 2.0) # normal distribution with mean value 12 and standard deviation 2.

samp = sampler(ndist)   # sampler based on the ndist distribution

val1 = next(samp)       # A random value from ndist distribution
val2 = next(samp)       # Another random value from ndist distribution
val3 = next(samp)       # Yet another random value from ndist distribution

  • cv (float) –

    Coefficient of variation of the log-normal distribution.

Returns:

  • Generator –

    A log-normal distribution sampler with given mean value and coefficient of variation.

Example

The following example creates a Log-Normal distribution sampler and generates three realizations.

samp = lognorm_sampler(12.0, 0.25)  # log-normal sampler with
                                    # mean value 12.0 and CoV = 0.25.

val1 = next(samp)   # A random value from the log-normal distribution
val2 = next(samp)   # Another random value from the log-normal distribution
val3 = next(samp)   # Yet another random value from the log-normal distribution

docs.title: standard_gap_sampler
docs.text:
standard_gap_sampler(flange_diameter, flange_flatness_tolerance, gap_angle_sampler=lognorm_sampler(100 * deg, 1.0), gap_shape_factor_sampler=norm_sampler(1.0, 0.15), gap_height_cap=2.0)

Sampler that generates random flange gaps according to IEC 61400-6 AMD1.

For each realization, a gap angle is drawn from gap_angle_sampler, the gap height is then drawn from the distribution returned by gap_height_distribution for that angle (ref. [2], section 6.7.5.2), and the gap shape factor is drawn from gap_shape_factor_sampler. Realizations are discarded and redrawn when the gap angle is not between 0 and 180 degrees, or when the gap height exceeds gap_height_cap times the 95th percentile of its distribution.

The default shape factor distribution, N(1.0, 0.15), is the one of the stochastic model of ref. [1], Table 7. In ref. [5] (section 6.4.6) the shape factor is no longer used, because the shape effects are included in the ED2 gap height distribution (see standard_gap_sampler_ED2).

Parameters:

  • flange_diameter (float) –

    The outer diameter of the flange, in meters.

  • flange_flatness_tolerance (float) –

    The flatness tolerance in mm/mm.

  • gap_angle_sampler (Generator, default: lognorm_sampler(100 * deg, 1.0) ) –

    A sampler for the gap angle, in radians. Defaults to a log-normal sampler with mean 100 deg and CoV = 1.0.

  • gap_shape_factor_sampler (Generator, default: norm_sampler(1.0, 0.15) ) –

    A sampler for the gap shape factor. Defaults to a normal sampler with mean 1.0 and CoV = 0.15.

  • gap_height_cap (float, default: 2.0 ) –

    The generated gap height will be capped at gap_height_cap * p95, where p95 is the 95th percentile of the gap height distribution. If omitted, it defaults to 2.0.

Yields:

  • Gap –

    A random gap, with random height, angle and shape factor.

Example

The following example creates a standard gap sampler and generates three realizations.

# Gap sampler for a 7.5 m flange with flatness tolerance 1.4 mm/m
samp = standard_gap_sampler(7.5, 0.0014)

gap1 = next(samp)  # A random gap
gap2 = next(samp)  # Another random gap
gap3 = next(samp)  # Yet another random gap

print(gap1.height, gap1.angle, gap1.shape_factor)

    A random gap, with random height and angle.

# ED2 gap sampler for a 7.5 m flange with flatness tolerance 1.4 mm/m
samp = standard_gap_sampler_ED2(7.5, 0.0014)
gap = next(samp)

docs.title: clayton_copula_sampler
docs.text:
clayton_copula_sampler(theta, marginal_dist1, marginal_dist2)

Sampler of two random variables joined by a Clayton copula.

The copula realizations are generated with the conditional inverse method: given two independent uniform variables u and w, the second copula variable is

\[v = \left(u^{-\theta} \left(w^{-\theta/(1+\theta)} - 1\right) + 1\right)^{-1/\theta}\]

and the two variables are then mapped to the marginal distributions via their inverse cumulative distribution functions. The Kendall's rank correlation of the two variables is \(\tau = \theta / (\theta + 2)\).

Parameters:

  • theta (float) –

    Clayton copula parameter. Must be positive.

  • marginal_dist1 (rv_frozen) –

    Marginal distribution of the first variable.

  • marginal_dist2 (rv_frozen) –

    Marginal distribution of the second variable.

Yields:

  • ndarray –

    An array [x1, x2] containing a joint realization of the two variables.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If theta is not positive.

Example 
from scipy.stats import norm, lognorm
samp = clayton_copula_sampler(2.0, norm(10, 1), lognorm(0.5))
x1, x2 = next(samp)
